title: Running time of the gate clause machine
statement: There is a finite-state multi-tape Turing machine that, on every Boolean input of length $n$, halts with output equal to the gate-clause encoding of that input and uses exactly $200(n+1)^2$ units of time.
hypotheses_covered: Input is any finite list of Boolean symbols
The time bound is $200(n+1)^2$, where $n$ is the input length
The machine halts and outputs the specified encoding
The machine uses some natural-number amount of space
